champion: Vascular tumor associated with a somatic KDR mutation
ordered_diagnoses: Vascular tumor associated with a somatic KDR mutation

s1.syndrome_frame: cutaneous vascular lesion with telangiectasias in a patient with metastatic cancer
salient_findings: single, well-defined, blanchable bright red plaque on the lower right lateral shin
discrete clusters of small-caliber vessels on histopathological analysis
key_facts: patient is a man in his 40s
patient has stage IV KRAS wild-type rectal adenocarcinoma
patient has pulmonary and liver metastases
patient has undergone radiation therapy and multiple chemotherapy cycles
lesion appeared in early January 2015
lesion is not associated with pain or pruritus
lesion is 4 cm in diameter
histopathological analysis shows superficial, small lobules of small-caliber vessels
epidermis is normal
somatic mutation in KDR (VEGFR2) gene is identified as c.C2312G, p.T771R

raw.rationale: The presence of a somatic mutation in the KDR (VEGFR2) gene, identified as c.C2312G, p.T771R, along with the histopathological findings of superficial, small lobules of small-caliber vessels, supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Angiosarcoma
rejected.why: Angiosarcoma typically presents with more aggressive features and atypical cells, which is not consistent with the normal epidermis and discrete clusters of small-caliber vessels observed in this case.

rejected.label: Radiation-induced angiosarcoma
rejected.why: While the patient has undergone radiation therapy, there is no direct evidence linking the radiation to the development of the vascular lesion, and the timing does not strongly support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Chemotherapy-induced angiosarcoma
rejected.why: Similar to radiation-induced angiosarcoma, the link between chemotherapy and the development of this specific type of lesion is not clearly established in this case, and other factors such as the KDR mutation are more directly implicated.

rejected.label: Glomeruloid hemangioma
rejected.why: Glomeruloid hemangiomas are typically associated with POEMS syndrome, and the clinical presentation and histological findings in this case do not align with the characteristic features of glomeruloid hemangiomas.
